given: an existing stock row whose inventory_code does not parse into distinct batch and serial segments (e.g. "X-1" or a bare "c")
when: the up migration runs its backfill
then: that row's missing batch_number and/or serial_number are set to NULL rather than a guessed value, the row itself is retained (never dropped), and the migration does not raise on the non-conforming code
architectural_notes: Infra contract realized by PI2-batch-serial-nullable: because batch_number and serial_number are NULLABLE, a short/malformed code backfills to NULL instead of a fabricated value or a lost row, and the migration tolerates it without raising. Verified by an R4/NFR-F6-4 real-branch integration test seeding malformed codes and asserting NULL segments, row retention, and no error.

independence.rationale: AC1 asserts correct extraction from a well-formed code; AC2 asserts the non-conforming branch (NULL-not-guess, row retained, no raise). The malformed path can break (a guessed value, a dropped row, or a raised error) while well-formed extraction still works, and vice versa
